meta.title: How a route gets chosen and switched (one check)

messages.label: position + heading
messages.note: Every 60 s of drive time. Real GPS (live drive mode) is in progress.

messages.label: driving-traffic request
messages.note: From the car position, heading with 45 degrees either side.

messages.label: up to 3 RouteCandidates
messages.note: adapter.ts: ETA, typical time, intersections, freeway stretches.

messages.label: signal points + missing tiles
messages.note: Chain: bundled tiles, device cache, Overpass backup.

messages.label: withSignalCounts, rankRoutes
messages.note: Best ETA first. Signals only break ties of 30 s or less.

messages.label: state + this check + thresholds
messages.note: Pure: same inputs, same answer. Rules in the card below.

messages.label: new route + spoken reason
messages.note: Example: Switching: saves 3 minutes, turn in 0.8 miles. Voice is in progress.

cards.title: A switch needs ALL of these (DEFAULT_REROUTE_OPTIONS)
items: Saves at least 120 s AND at least 5% of the time left
Turn-off at least 400 m and 20 s ahead (1200 m for a freeway exit)
The same alternative wins 2 checks in a row
No switch within 300 s of the last one
Going back to a route left under 600 s ago needs 2x the saving

cards.title: Special cases
items: Off route (fresh routes start over 50 m from the line): take the best route at once
Current route no longer offered: wait 3 checks, then take the best
Failed check or missing traffic data: stay
Same-route test is by path within 10 m, never by route id

cards.title: Where signals come in
items: Alternatives are tried in ranking order
Signal count only breaks ETA ties of 30 s or less
A partial or unknown count has no say
Signals never justify a switch on their own
